newsitem.title: UK: IBCA affirms British Land ratings.
newsitem.headline: IBCA affirms British Land ratings.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Monday it affirmed the long-term and short-term ratings of The British Land Company Plc at BBB plus and A2 respectively.
"British Land was assigned the BBB plus rating on March 19, 1996 after the company assumed 100 percent ownership of Broadgate Properties Plc," IBCA said in a statement.

"This acquisition placed financial pressures upon British Land in terms of gearing (FY96 120 percent FY95 93 percent) and interest coverage (FY96 1.5x FY95 1.6x) despite the equity issue in December 1995," IBCA said.
Broadgate also increased British Land's exposure to City of London offices to 40 percent of the group portfolio, IBCA said.
"The underlying assets within British Land's portfolio are strong, with long-dated leases and quality tenants securing the income stream," it said.
However, Broadgate diluted financial coverages compared with pre-acquisition levels and the resultant increase in debt has increased headline gearing, it said.
"The fundamentals of British Land's financial profile should improve on FY96, but gearing at 120 percent (IBCA calculation) restrains the company's financial flexibility," IBCA said.
"Maximum gearing under bond covenants is 175 percent, British Lands's YE96 actual being around 115 percent (bond covenant calculation)," IBCA said.
